info.title: WtF API
info.description:
Version 1 of the API, served under /api/v1. Within a version the API only
grows (new routes, optional fields, fields in answers); every answer names
the current revision in the `API-Revision` header. A breaking change would
become /api/v2, served next to /api/v1 for a while. A request for a
version the server doesn't serve gets an `unsupported-api-version`
problem that lists the versions it does serve (`supported`). The
refactor of 2026-11-01 changed /api/v1 in place, once, and its revision
started again at 1 (WTFD.md, "Versions").

Where to Find: a register of the things you own and where they are.
Every endpoint calls one database function; see API.md for the semantics
and WTFD.md for the HTTP conventions.

- Numbers of attributes and items with a unit are given and stored in the
  base unit of the unit's quantity; responses add a `display` value in the
  best-scaling unit of the unit's family, or in the unit itself when
  `unit_lock` is set.
- Outside the unit routes a unit is its id: clients keep the unit families
  (`GET /unit-families`, revalidated by `ETag`) and look units up there,
  as they keep the class and location trees.
- The hostname picks the inventory: its first label is a tenant's host
  ("bob" for bob.wtf.example), see TENANTS.md. A hostname that picks none
  gets 404 from every route that needs a session, or from /login.
- Everything has UUIDs as ids. Quantities, unit families and units are
  global (every tenant sees them) or the tenant's own, and a tenant can
  turn quantities and families off.
- Every account has a role (ACCOUNTS.md): a `viewer` reads everything
  but the accounts; a `user` also changes items and stock rows (with
  their values and attachments); an `admin` also sets up locations,
  classes, attributes and units, imports and exports model files, and
  manages accounts. History of items and stock rows is for every account,
  the rest for admins. A request the role doesn't allow gets 403.
- A field the server needs is required in a request body, even if as
  null; nothing is assumed.
- Errors are RFC 9457 problem details (`application/problem+json`).
- `GET /classes`, `GET /locations` and `GET /unit-families` support
  `ETag` / `If-None-Match`.
- POST /login sets the session cookie `wtf_session` (HttpOnly,
  SameSite=Strict, Path=/api); send it back with every request. Only
  /api/health, /api/v1/openapi and /login work without it; a request
  without it gets 401 at once. Requests that change something are
  refused (403) when their Origin header names another site.

get.summary: One quantity with the unit families the tenant sees, each with its units

patch.summary: Turn a quantity on or off for the tenant (admins)
patch.description:
Turning a quantity off turns its families off too. A quantity whose
units live attributes or items use can't be turned off (409).

post.summary: Import units, attributes and classes from a model file (admins)
post.description:
The body is a model file (seed/model-format.md): quantities with their
unit families and units, attributes, and a tree of classes with their
attribute assignments. What the tenant has (or sees, for units) and
is the same is used as it is; what isn't there is added, as the
tenant's own; what differs is a conflict. An assignment that is the
same as one the class inherits is there already. All or nothing: with
a conflict, or with dry_run, nothing is kept. A body that isn't a
valid model file is refused with 400. A file of only quantities is
how units are imported.

parameters.name: parent
parameters.description: The class to import below; the top of the class tree without it.

parameters.name: dry_run
parameters.description: true: nothing is kept, and the report says what would be. Absent: false.

200.description: What was (or would be) added, what was there already, and the conflicts.

get.summary: The unit families the tenant sees, with their units
get.description: Every unit family the tenant sees, with its units. Clients keep them, and ask again with If-None-Match: 304 when unchanged.

get.summary: One unit family with its units, smallest first

patch.summary: Turn a unit family on or off for the tenant (admins)
patch.description:
A family of a quantity that is turned off stays off. A family whose
units live attributes or items use can't be turned off (409).

delete.summary: Mark a class deleted; with recursive=true also every class below it
delete.description:
Without `recursive`, the class must have no subclasses or items (else 409).
With `recursive=true`, the class and every class below it are deleted in one
transaction. If any of them has items, nothing is deleted (409), unless `force=true`,
which deletes the items too (with their values, stock rows and attachments).
`GET /classes/{id}/deletion` previews it.

get.summary: The class with everything below it, as a model file (admins)
get.description:
A model file (seed/model-format.md) of the class and the live classes
below it, with the class's inherited assignments as its own, every
attribute they use, and the units of the tenant's own those attributes
need, with their families. Units every WtF has are left out. "meta"
names the class, the tenant and when. Importing the file where the
class is changes nothing; importing it elsewhere sets up the same.

get.summary: What a recursive delete of the class would delete; deletes nothing
get.description:
Needs the same role as the delete. Unlike the delete, it reports items
without `force` instead of failing.

put.summary: Assign an attribute to a class, or change its default

default.description: Optional default in the attribute's datatype (numbers in the base unit); null for none.

scope.description: Where its values live: on the item, or on each stock row.

required.description: New items (or stock rows, for per-unit attributes) need a value unless there is a default.

delete.summary: Remove an attribute from a class

parameters.name: class
parameters.description: Only items in this class or its subclasses.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description:
Words separated by spaces. Every word must occur, as a case-insensitive
substring, in the item name, a class in the item's class path, a text
or url value, or a choice value (including class defaults the item
shows). Different words may match in different places, so
"resistor 0805" finds 0805 resistors.

parameters.name: where
parameters.description:
Attribute filters, all of which must match: a JSON list of
{attribute, op, value}. Numbers and dates take =, >, >=, <, <= or
between [low, high] (numbers in the base unit); text and url take
= or contains; choices take = (one option) or in (a list), by id
or name; booleans take = true or false. Compared with the values
the item shows, class defaults included; a per-unit attribute
matches when any live stock row does. See api/item.md.

delete.description:
Without `recursive`, the location must have no sublocations or stock (else 409).
With `recursive=true`, the location and every location below it are deleted in one
transaction. If there is stock in any of them, nothing is deleted (409), unless
`force=true`, which deletes those stock rows too. `GET /locations/{id}/deletion`
previews it.

without `force` instead of failing.

exactly one counted row of the same item, the amount is merged into it.

delete.description: If it was the photo, there is no photo any more, also after a restore. It is purged with "wtfd deleted purge"; then "wtfd gc" removes its file once no attachment has its hash.

post.summary: Restore a deleted attachment of an item (the object must not be deleted)
post.description: It comes back as an ordinary attachment, not as the photo it may have been.

get.summary: The content of an attachment of an item
get.description:
Images (except SVG), PDF and plain text are sent inline, everything
else as a download, named after the title with an extension for the
type. The ETag is the SHA-256 of the content, which never changes;
Range requests are supported.

client.description: What the client calls itself ("WtF on Pixel 9"), for the list of sessions.

max_idle.description: Seconds the session may sit unused before it expires; null: never.

200.description:
Logged in. The session is in the cookie `wtf_session`, never in the body;
it expires after 30 days without use, and every answer renews it.

Set-Cookie.description: wtf_session=<token>; Path=/api; Max-Age=2592000; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict (and Secure over HTTPS)

429.description: Too many failed logins; one attempt per minute until a login succeeds.

post.summary: End the current session

204.description: Logged out; the session cookie is deleted.

put.summary: Change the own password (ends all other sessions)

end_other_sessions.description: Whether the account's other sessions end too.

post.summary: Create an account (admins)

password.description: Without a password the account can't log in.

patch.description: Changing the password ends the account's sessions. You can't change your own role.

password.description: null removes the password (the account can't log in).

end_sessions.description: With password, and only with it: whether the account's sessions end too. Not for one's own account.

delete.summary: Delete an account (admins; not your own)
delete.description: The account is marked deleted (history keeps referring to it); its email can be used again.

get.description: The item, its values, its stock rows and their per-unit values, and the attachments of the item and its stock rows. Newest first; also for deleted objects. Every account may read it.
The row, its per-unit values and its attachments. Newest first; also for deleted objects. Every account may read it.

The location, stock rows that were there (including arrivals and departures), its attachments, and the locations directly inside it being added, moved in or out, deleted, restored or purged. Newest first; also for deleted objects. For admins.

The class, its attribute assignments, its attachments, and the classes directly below it and its items being added, moved in or out, deleted, restored or purged. Newest first; also for deleted objects. For admins.
The attribute and its options. Newest first; also for deleted objects. For admins.
Changes to the account itself. Newest first; also for deleted objects. For admins.
Top-level locations being added, moved to or from the top level, deleted, restored or purged, so that a deleted one can be found. Newest first. For admins.
Top-level classes being added, moved to or from the top level, deleted, restored or purged, so that a deleted one can be found. Newest first. For admins.
Attributes being added, deleted, restored or purged, so that a deleted one can be found. Newest first. For admins.

The sessions of the account the request is made with, most recently used first.

parameters.description: The session's id, as GET /me/sessions gives it.

session.name: wtf_session
session.description: The session cookie set by POST /login.

API-Revision.description: The revision of API version 1 the server implements; it grows with every addition.

Force.name: force
Force.description: With recursive: also delete what uses the deleted nodes (items of classes, stock at locations).

IfNoneMatch.name: If-None-Match
IfNoneMatch.description: The ETag of the tree the client already has.

Before.name: before
Before.description: The id of the oldest entry the client has; the page is the entries older than it. Absent: from the newest. History pages refuse offset.

file.description: The file; its Content-Type is kept (and detected when missing or application/octet-stream).

photo.description: Make it the object's photo (images only).

parent.description: Parent node; none for a root.

container.description: Holds only other classes (no items) or locations (no stock).

confirm.description: Needed for a grid of more than 1000 locations.

schema.description: grid is for locations only, and required there (null: none).

parent.description: New parent; null makes it a root.

container.description: Rejected (422) while the class has items or the location has stock.

photo.description: One of its own image attachments, or null for none.

History.description: One page of history entries, newest first.

AttachmentCreated.description: Created. `Location` points at the attachment, under its object.

UnitFamilies.description: The unit families with their version.

stock.description: Number of stock rows of those items.
The live stock rows; for a deleted item, those deleted together with it.

hint.description: What to do about it, when the database knows (revision 2).

sqlstate.description: PostgreSQL error code, when the error came from the database.

place_key.description: restore-into-deleted only: the request field that restores it somewhere else (class, parent or location).

with_parents.description: restore-into-deleted only: true, as "with_parents": true restores what it is in too.

name.description: A new name, for when the old one has been taken since.

parent.description: Restore it under this parent instead; null at the top.

with_parents.description: Also restore the deleted nodes it is in.

name.description: A new name, for when the old one has been taken since.

Deleted.description: null for a live object; for a deleted one, the action that deleted it, when, and by whom (null: wtfd itself). Lists and trees leave deleted objects out; fetching one by id or code still works.

base_unit.description: The unit numbers are stored in (factor 1, offset 0), in the same lists.

global.description: Every tenant sees it; otherwise it is the tenant's own.

available.description: Lists and gets of quantities only: whether the tenant can choose its units.

standard.description: Lists and gets of quantities only: available when the tenant hasn't chosen (always true for its own).

choice.description: Lists and gets of quantities only: the tenant's choice; null follows the default.

available.description: true or false; null follows the default again.

added.description: 'Names; families as "Quantity › Family", units as "Quantity › Family › symbol"; classes as paths ("MCU/AVR"); assignments as "path: attribute".'

global.description: Every tenant sees it; otherwise it is the tenant's own.
Every tenant sees it; otherwise it is the tenant's own.

available.description: Whether the tenant can choose its units; never while its quantity is off.

standard.description: Available when the tenant hasn't chosen (always true for its own).

choice.description: The tenant's choice; null follows the default.

units.description: The ones the tenant sees, smallest first.

id.description: Newer entries have higher ids; the next page goes before the oldest one.

action.description: The call the change was part of: entries of one call share it.

table.description: e.g. item, item_value, stock, stock_value, location, attachment.

data.description: The row after the change (before it, for a delete).

Role.description: Each role can do what the ones before it can (ACCOUNTS.md).

deleted.description: Deleted accounts can't log in; they stay visible because history refers to them.

Attachments.description: The photo first, then by title.

Values.description: Own values plus class defaults (is_default) where there is no own value.

value.description: The value in the attribute's datatype; numbers in the base unit of the attribute's unit.

is_default.description: The class default, shown because there is no own value.

Missing.description: Required attributes without a value (and without a default).

Display.description: A base-unit number in the best-scaling unit of the family, or in the unit itself with unit_lock.

options.description: Only for choice attributes in GET /attributes/{id}: its live options, by name.

photo.description: The class or location photo, or null.

container.description: Holds only other classes, no items.

default.description: The default in the attribute's datatype, or null.

scope.description: Where its values live: on the item, or on each stock row.

container.description: Holds only other locations, no stock.

incomplete.description: The item or one of its stock rows lacks a required value.

amount.description: In the base unit of the item's unit (counted if none); null: present, not counted.

merged_into.description: For a row a move merged into another, that row.

photo.description: The stock row photo, or null.

UnitMember.description: A unit in its family's list, without its family and quantity. base = value × base_factor + base_offset.

global.description: Every tenant sees it; otherwise it is the tenant's own.

id.description: The token's SHA-256, in hex; it can't be turned back into the token.

client.description: What the client called itself when logging in.

last_used.description: Written at most once a minute.

max_idle.description: Seconds it may sit unused; null: never expires.

usage.description: The last 8 addresses it was used from, newest first.
